From dfbc282c2e16cd6044e4181f150dbd1e2224eaa7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2014 11:49:17 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] check multiple parser methods are not defined in a parser

This fixes a bug introduced in be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf.

The old commit(be4a21) checked only the case that allparser, parser2 and parser_with_gc
were not set but didn't check more than one were set. This patch checks this case, too.

Signed-off-by: Masatake YAMATO <yamato@redhat.com>

diff --git a/parse.c b/parse.c
index 557228d1d..2ae586ea0 100644
--- a/parse.c
+++ b/parse.c
@@ -969,7 +969,7 @@ extern void initializeParsing (void)
 				accepted = TRUE;
 #endif
 			}
-			else if ((def->parser == NULL)  &&  (def->parser2 == NULL) && (def->parser_with_gc == NULL))
+			else if (((!!def->parser) + (!!def->parser2) + (!!def->parser_with_gc)) != 1)
 				error (FATAL,
 		"%s parser definition must define one and only one parsing routine\n",
 					   def->name);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: parse.c**
- The conditional check in the `initializeParsing` function was modified. 
- The original check verified that all three parser methods (`parser`, `parser2`, and `parser_with_gc`) were not set to `NULL`. 
- The new check ensures that exactly one of these parser methods is defined (i.e., not `NULL`). It uses a sum of boolean values to count how many of the parser methods are defined and checks that this sum equals one.

### Relationships
- The modification in `parse.c` addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (be4a2117494ce73750cec3fd3c7cb4a60e722bcf) that only checked if all parser methods were unset. The new logic ensures that the parser definitions are validated correctly, enforcing that only one parser method can be defined at a time, thus preventing potential conflicts or undefined behavior in the parsing process.
